{{- /* The corporate footer: marketing's content, this theme's look. Content is marketing's and is not authored here. The structure comes from the same footer-definition-new.json feed that www.gooddata.ai, docs/cloud and the shared gooddata-docs-theme render (ported from gooddata/gooddata-docs-theme@bd047764d2c1, WEB-4512): the banner with its "Ask AI" caption, provider buttons and CTA links, the six link columns, the legal line and the social row. As upstream does, the `subscribe` banner action is dropped, because the newsletter modal it opens belongs to the marketing site. The look is ours. Marketing's Footer.css is not loaded: every element here uses the theme's Tailwind tokens (bg-gd-surface, border-gd-border, text-gd-text-secondary, ...), so the footer follows light and dark mode like the header strip above the page. The feed's social icons and the provider icons are marketing's dark 48px tiles; .gd-footer-icon in main.css.tmpl hides the tile and paints the glyph in currentColor, so they sit in the same bordered boxes as the header controls. Below lg each link column is a disclosure: a button (aria-expanded) and a list that footer-accordion.js shows and hides. At lg every list is shown by `lg:block` whatever the button says, so with JS off a desktop reader loses nothing and a phone shows the headings. The banner title is emitted with safeHTML because the feed carries a `
` in it, as the upstream theme does. The snapshot test pins that titles hold no other markup. The
carries Bootstrap classes (d-none d-md-block) that mean nothing here; it is a plain line break. Content sources, in order: 1. `site.Params.footerDefinitionURL`, fetched at build time. 2. `data/footer.json` in this theme — a committed snapshot of that feed. The snapshot is what makes the fetch safe to depend on. A marketing-side outage, a runner with no egress, a 404 or a schema change that fails to unmarshal all fall back to it with a warning instead of failing the build. Refresh it with: curl -sSL https://www.gooddata.ai/learn-assets/js/footer-definition-new.json \ | python3 -m json.tool --no-ensure-ascii > themes/gd-docs-theme-next/data/footer.json The feed is served from gooddata.ai; the old .com URL 301s there, so pointing at .com costs every build a redirect for the same bytes. */ -}} {{- $def := dict -}} {{- with hugo.Data.footer }}{{ $def = .footer }}{{ end -}} {{- with site.Params.footerDefinitionURL -}} {{- $url := . -}} {{- $fetch := try (resources.GetRemote $url) -}} {{- with $fetch.Err -}} {{- warnf "footer: %q could not be fetched (%s); falling back to the vendored snapshot" $url . -}} {{- else -}} {{- /* try owns the error path: a non-200, a DNS failure and a timeout all land in $fetch.Err, and the resource it yields has no .Err of its own to consult. */ -}} {{- with $fetch.Value -}} {{- $parse := try (transform.Unmarshal .) -}} {{- with $parse.Err -}} {{- warnf "footer: %q is not valid JSON (%s); falling back to the vendored snapshot" $url . -}} {{- else -}} {{- with $parse.Value.footer -}}{{ $def = . }}{{- end -}} {{- end -}} {{- else -}} {{- /* A 404 yields no error and no resource, just nil — so without this branch a feed that has been dead for months falls back silently and the footer quietly ages. */ -}} {{- warnf "footer: %q returned no content (404 or empty body); falling back to the vendored snapshot" $url -}} {{- end -}} {{- end -}} {{- end -}}
{{- /* href="#top" needs no #top element: the HTML spec special-cases that fragment to mean the top of the document. */}} Skip footer content
